The Signed Agreement remains unchanged and takes precedence. ## Agreement Governance Protocol For Puretronics, the signed Services Agreement dated **9 July 2026** is the first authority for legal scope, commercial terms, exclusions, deliverables, and approval/scope-change rules. The Product Master Database is the governed product-intelligence source, not the legal or commercial source of truth. Use this order before proposal, funnel, campaign, or commercial work: 1. Check the signed Services Agreement for covered products, exclusions, commercial terms, and scope-control rules. 2. Use the aligned Annexure A/B pages for funnel and commercial interpretation. 3. Use the Product Master Database for product intelligence, technical reference, buyer problems, sales positioning, and source/spec governance. 4. Treat laser accessories, spark tester fault-intelligence/accessory items, and loadcell accessories as support items only. 5. Do not create or imply standalone pages, campaigns, forms, automations, SEO, selectors, calculators, configurators, export/OEM/partner/multilingual expansion, or extra product pages for support items unless separately approved in writing. --- # Guide Purpose This guide explains how to navigate and use the `Puretronics Wire & Cable Product Master Database` without ambiguity. After reading it, a human user or AI agent should know what the database contains, which view to use, how to interpret each field, how to extract sales and technical intelligence, and how to avoid unsafe claims. The database is designed for Puretronics Wire and Cable Industry product intelligence. It supports sales discovery, proposal writing, funnel architecture, product comparison, line-stage mapping, cross-sell planning, technical lookup, and source-governed quotation support. It does not override the signed Services Agreement for contracted scope, commercials, exclusions, deliverables, or change-control decisions. Primary database: [Puretronics Wire & Cable Product Master Database](/p/c303dd29567d83f9bfc301995427e6e7?pvs=25) # Core Mental Model The database is one master table, not a collection of disconnected product sheets. Each row represents a product, model/variant, accessory group, or system. Each property adds one layer of intelligence: - Identity fields tell you what the row is. - Sales fields explain why a buyer should care. - Technical fields describe what the product measures, controls, tests, inputs, outputs, or integrates with. - Navigation fields place the row in manufacturing flow, product family, solution theme, funnel stage, and proposal use. - Governance fields warn you when specs are complete, variant-dependent, source-limited, or must be verified at quotation. The database is optimized for product/model rows. Broad product families are represented through grouping fields and views, not separate databases. # First 5 Minutes Use this sequence when entering the database for the first time: 1. Open `01 Sales Snapshot` to understand the portfolio in plain commercial terms. 2. Open `02 Manufacturing Flow` to see where each product sits in a wire/cable line. 3. Open `04 Product Family Navigator` to compare the five canonical families: Inline Measurement & Dimensional Control; Inline Spark Testing & Insulation Fault Detection; Cable Testing & Validation; Process Equipment & Line Auxiliaries; and Tension, Braking & Line Control. 4. Open `06 Technical Lookup` only when you need ranges, power, interfaces, standards, caveats, or configuration details. 5. Open `10 Source & Spec Governance` before using a spec in a quote, proposal, technical email, or AI-generated claim. # Row Types
Row Type Meaning How To Use
`Product` A standalone Puretronics product with its own commercial and technical identity. Use for product positioning, discovery, proposals, and technical lookup.
`Model / Variant` A specific model within a platform or family. Use for comparison, sizing, range selection, and quotation conversations.
`Accessory` A supporting item or accessory group with sales or qualification value. Use for add-ons, integration completeness, and cross-sell logic.
`System` A larger configured solution or compliance test system. Use for solution selling, compliance conversations, and technical qualification.
Do not treat accessory rows as full product rows unless the row itself carries a buyer problem, CTA, and technical reason to discuss it. # Field Dictionary ## Core Identity
Field Meaning Operating Rule
`Product / Model Name` Stable row name. Use this as the unique row key when referring to products.
`Product Family` Highest-level portfolio grouping. Use for family navigation and proposal sectioning.
`Product Type` Functional category such as Gauge, Controller, Tester, Preheater, Brake, Loadcell, Accessory, or System. Use for technical comparison and view grouping.
`Row Type` Defines whether the row is a product, model/variant, accessory, or system. Check this before assuming row importance.
`Parent Product / Platform` Product platform or family. Use to connect variants back to their umbrella platform.
`Model / Variant` Model number or variant name. Use for quotation and technical matching.
`Source Coverage` Source reference or reference-section coverage. Use to trace the origin of product intelligence.
## Navigation And Taxonomy
Field Meaning Operating Rule
`Manufacturing Flow Stage` Ordered wire/cable line stage. Use this for process sequence. It is the authoritative flow field.
`Production / Context Tags` Flexible process, QA, compliance, data, or application tags. Use this for broad filtering, not sequence.
`Solution Theme` Commercial solution taxonomy. Use this for funnel architecture, bundles, and buyer-problem clustering.
`Sales Priority` Commercial emphasis: Hero, Strategic, Supporting, or Niche. Use Hero rows as proposal anchors.
`Industry 4.0 Relevance` Degree of connectivity, data, reporting, HMI, ERP, or communication relevance. Use High for connected-factory messaging.
`Line Integration Complexity` Expected implementation complexity. Use High rows for technical calls and line audits.
`Funnel Stage Fit` Sales funnel stages where the row is useful. Use for campaign and funnel planning.
`Proposal Section Fit` Proposal sections where the row belongs. Use when assembling proposal architecture.
## Buyer And Sales Intelligence
Field Meaning Operating Rule
`Primary Buyer Problem` The pain or operational issue the product addresses. Start sales copy here.
`Best-Fit Customer Question` The buyer question the product best answers. Use in discovery scripts and proposal framing.
`Primary Use Case` Practical use of the product. Use for concise summaries.
`Target Personas` Buyer and influencer personas. Use to tailor messaging.
`Core Buyer Value` Outcome the buyer gets. Use in executive summaries.
`Differentiators` Mechanism-specific reasons to care. Use only when tied to the product mechanism.
`Discovery Questions` Questions to ask the prospect. Use in calls, audits, and qualification.
`Recommended CTA` Next best action. Use to guide sales motion.
`Proposal Positioning` How to frame the product in proposals. Use for proposal paragraphs and section logic.
`Cross-Sell / Complementary Products` Related rows that pair with this row. Use to build bundles and solution sets.
`Notes For Sales Team` Practical selling guidance. Use for internal sales enablement.
## Technical Intelligence
Field Meaning Operating Rule
`Measured / Controlled Parameter` What the product measures, controls, tests, or applies. Use for technical matching.
`Material / Cable Applicability` Applicable material, cable type, or process class. Use to qualify fit.
`Range / Capacity` Measurement range, OD, capacity, voltage, torque, or similar limit. Treat as quote-sensitive when `Spec Confidence` warns you.
`Speed / Throughput` Line speed, scan speed, test speed, or throughput. Use for high-speed-line qualification.
`Power Supply` Electrical or pneumatic supply. Confirm before quotation.
`Inputs` Required sensor, product, signal, utility, or process inputs. Use for integration planning.
`Outputs` Alarms, signals, relay outputs, reports, brake outputs, or process outputs. Use for automation and QA discussions.
`Communication / Integration` RS485, Modbus, Ethernet, TCP/IP, Wi-Fi, ERP, PLC, HMI, or software integration. Use for Industry 4.0 and controls conversations.
`Display / UI` Operator interface details. Use when discussing usability and line visibility.
`Safety / Compliance / Standards` Standards, interlocks, CE/ATEX, door interlocks, fire standards, or safety notes. Use carefully and check `Spec Confidence`.
`Operating Conditions` Environment, physical limits, or process notes. Use for fit checks.
`Dimensions` Physical dimensions. Confirm before layout or quotation.
`Weight` Product weight. Confirm for installation planning.
`Accessories / Options` Optional accessories and add-ons. Use for completeness and cross-sell.
`Important Caveats` Conflicts, variant notes, source limitations, or verification needs. Read before using technical claims.
`Spec Confidence` Confidence level for technical use. This is the governing field for claim safety.
# Manufacturing Flow Stages Use `Manufacturing Flow Stage` when you need ordered process logic. The numbering exists so Notion grouping stays in production order.
Stage Meaning Typical Puretronics Coverage
`01 Pay-off / Unwind` Material feeding and unwinding. Tension measurement/control, braking, loadcells.
`02 Joining / Butt Welding` Conductor joining or repair. Butt Welding Machine.
`03 Tension & Braking Control` Tension sensing, monitoring, braking, and closed-loop control. WTI, LTC-PRO, loadcells, amplifiers, pneumatic brakes.
`04 Pre-extrusion / Preheating` Conductor preparation before insulation. Inline Induction Wire Preheater variants.
`05 Powdering / Talc Application` Controlled powder/talc coating. LSP-G1 and LSP-G2 Static Powder Applicators.
`06 Extrusion / Coating` Insulation/coating process context. Laser measurement and related line equipment context.
`07 Cooling` Cooling after extrusion. Context stage for post-extrusion inspection readiness.
`08 Online Measurement` Non-contact online dimensional measurement. LASER 2008, LASER 2000, LASER-H, accessories.
`09 Spark / Fault Inspection` Online insulation fault detection. Live Spark, Acute Spark, DC Spark.
`10 Inline Marking` Physical marking of detected defects. Spark Tester IoT Stage 3.
`11 Rewinding / Coiling` Rewind, coil, and final handling. Tension/braking products where applicable.
`12 Offline HV Testing` Offline high-voltage insulation validation. AC HV Tester, DC HV Tester.
`13 Fire / Compliance Testing` Fire/water/shock compliance testing. Fire Resistance Cable Testing System.
`14 Repair / Rework` Repair and rework context. Butt welding and support workflows.
`15 Calibration / Support` Calibration and equipment support. Spark Tester Sensitivity Calibrator and support accessories.
`16 Data / Reporting Layer` Analytics, reports, ERP/data integration, and fault intelligence. Spark IoT stages, connected measurement/control products.
# Solution Themes Use `Solution Theme` to cluster products by buyer problem and sales motion.
Theme Use It When
`Diameter / Ovality Control` The prospect cares about OD, ovality, width, thickness, scrap, tolerance, or online dimensional QA.
`Spark Fault Intelligence` The prospect cares about insulation defects, bare patches, pinholes, fault classification, or defect marking.
`Tension Control` The prospect cares about line tension, tension measurement, force sensing, closed-loop control, or material travel stability.
`Braking / Unwind-Rewind` The prospect cares about braking torque, unwind, rewind, coiling, pay-off, or dancer/brake integration.
`Pre-Extrusion Quality` The prospect cares about conductor preheating, adhesion, dielectric quality, line speed, or sleeving reduction.
`Powdering / Clean Shopfloor` The prospect cares about talc/powder consistency, reduced mess, powder recovery, or clean line operation.
`Offline HV Testing` The prospect cares about offline insulation validation for coils, drums, or finished products.
`Fire Compliance` The prospect cares about BS EN fire/water/shock survival testing and emergency cable compliance.
`Data / Reporting` The prospect cares about logging, reports, ERP, HMI, Modbus, Ethernet, Wi-Fi, alarms, or connected-factory visibility.
`Joining / Repair` The prospect cares about joining copper/aluminium conductors or repairing wire.
`Calibration / Support` The prospect cares about verifying equipment sensitivity, calibration, or supporting test reliability.
# Spec Confidence `Spec Confidence` prevents the database from creating false certainty.
Value Meaning Usage Rule
`Complete Source-Backed` The maintained source gives enough product/model detail for confident proposal use. You may use the spec, while still confirming commercial configuration before final quote.
`Variant-Dependent` Specs vary by model, voltage, capacity, speed, range, or configuration. Use the database for narrowing options, then verify final model details.
`Source-Limited` The row is useful but source detail is sparse, grouped, or accessory-level. Avoid hard technical claims beyond what the row states.
`Verify At Quotation` Final standards, compliance scope, configuration, or sizing must be confirmed commercially. Do not present as final without engineering/sales confirmation.
# View-By-View Navigation
View Use Case How To Read It
`00 Admin - All Properties` Maintenance and auditing. Use only when editing or checking full row completeness. It is intentionally dense.
`01 Sales Snapshot` Fast commercial overview. Read Product, Family, Priority, Flow Stage, Solution Theme, Buyer Problem, Value, and CTA.
`02 Manufacturing Flow` Process-line mapping. Move through groups from stage 01 to stage 16 to understand where each product fits.
`03 Buyer Discovery` Call preparation and qualification. Use personas, buyer problem, best-fit question, discovery questions, CTA, and sales notes.
`04 Product Family Navigator` Portfolio education. Compare products inside each family and understand commercial emphasis.
`05 Hero Products` Proposal anchors and funnel-first products. Start from these rows when creating a proposal or campaign structure.
`06 Technical Lookup` Specs and configuration. Use for ranges, power, inputs, outputs, interfaces, standards, dimensions, and caveats.
`07 Connected Factory / Industry 4.0` Automation and data conversations. Use for rows with high connectivity, reporting, UI, alarms, Modbus, Ethernet, Wi-Fi, ERP, or HMI value.
`08 Proposal & Funnel Builder` Funnel architecture and proposal assembly. Group by funnel stage and read proposal positioning plus section-fit fields.
`09 Cross-Sell & Bundles` Bundle creation. Read complementary products, accessories/options, parent platforms, and sales notes.
`10 Source & Spec Governance` Technical claim safety. Check source coverage, spec confidence, caveats, ranges, power, and sales notes before final claims.
`Context Tags` Flexible process/application filtering. Use only for non-sequential tags such as QA, Data Layer, Compliance, Inspection, or High-speed lines.
# Human Playbooks ## Create A Proposal 1. Start with `05 Hero Products` to identify anchors. 2. Open `04 Product Family Navigator` to fill supporting products. 3. Use `02 Manufacturing Flow` to structure the proposal around the buyer's line. 4. Pull language from `Primary Buyer Problem`, `Core Buyer Value`, and `Proposal Positioning`. 5. Use `06 Technical Lookup` for specs. 6. Finish with `10 Source & Spec Governance` to verify caveats and spec confidence. ## Prepare For A Discovery Call 1. Open `03 Buyer Discovery`. 2. Filter by `Product Family`, `Solution Theme`, or `Target Personas`. 3. Use `Best-Fit Customer Question` to frame the conversation. 4. Use `Discovery Questions` to qualify range, line speed, material, compliance, integration, and current pain. 5. Use `Recommended CTA` to define the next action. ## Build A Funnel Architecture 1. Open `08 Proposal & Funnel Builder`. 2. Group or filter by `Funnel Stage Fit`. 3. Use Hero rows for awareness and consideration assets. 4. Use technical and compliance rows for evaluation-stage content. 5. Use cross-sell rows for commercial discussion and expansion. 6. Use `Solution Theme` to create campaign clusters. ## Build A Cross-Sell Bundle 1. Open `09 Cross-Sell & Bundles`. 2. Start with the buyer's main product row. 3. Read `Cross-Sell / Complementary Products` and `Accessories / Options`. 4. Confirm technical compatibility in `06 Technical Lookup`. 5. Confirm caveats in `10 Source & Spec Governance`. ## Answer A Technical Question 1. Search the exact product or model name. 2. Open `06 Technical Lookup`. 3. Read `Range / Capacity`, `Speed / Throughput`, `Power Supply`, `Inputs`, `Outputs`, `Communication / Integration`, and `Safety / Compliance / Standards`. 4. Check `Important Caveats`. 5. Check `Spec Confidence` before writing or sending the answer. # AI-Agent Protocol An AI agent using this database must follow this order: 1. Identify the user intent: proposal, discovery, funnel, technical lookup, product comparison, cross-sell, or governance. 2. Choose the correct view based on the intent. 3. Use `Product / Model Name` as the row key. 4. Use `Manufacturing Flow Stage` for sequence and `Production / Context Tags` for flexible filtering. 5. Use `Solution Theme` for buyer-problem clustering. 6. Use `Sales Priority` to decide which rows should lead. 7. Use `Signed Scope Treatment`, `Signed Scope Note`, `Spec Confidence`, and `Important Caveats` before making any technical, funnel, proposal, or scope-sensitive claim. 8. If `Spec Confidence` is `Variant-Dependent`, `Source-Limited`, or `Verify At Quotation`, state that confirmation is required before final quotation. 9. Do not invent specs, standards, certifications, dimensions, weights, or integration details absent from the row. 10. Do not collapse WTI, Loadcells, Pneumatic Brakes, and LTC-PRO into one generic tension product. 11. Do not treat accessories or support items as primary products for signed-scope delivery. Support items cannot become standalone pages, campaigns, forms, automations, or assets unless separately approved in writing. 12. When asked for a final answer, synthesize from fields; do not paste every field unless the user asks for raw data. # Critical Product Distinctions
Product Area Correct Distinction
WTI Online tension measurement and indication.
Loadcells Force sensing/transducer layer for tension systems.
Pneumatic Brakes Braking actuator hardware for unwind/rewind control.
LTC-PRO Closed-loop web tension controller integrating sensor inputs, brake outputs, UI, communication, and alarms.
Spark Testers Core insulation fault detection equipment.
Spark IoT Accessories Fault classification, analytics, reporting, and inline marking layer.
Laser Gauges Non-contact dimensional measurement and tolerance control.
Laser Accessories Deployment, display, correction, and logging support.
HV Testers Offline insulation validation.
Fire Resistance System Compliance-grade fire/water/shock testing system.
# Maintenance Rules Use these rules when adding or editing rows: 1. Add a new row only when the item has independent sales, technical, model, accessory, or system value. 2. Do not create duplicate family rows if a model/variant row already carries the necessary intelligence. 3. Always fill `Product / Model Name`, `Product Family`, `Product Type`, `Row Type`, `Sales Priority`, `Manufacturing Flow Stage`, `Solution Theme`, and `Spec Confidence`. 4. Use `Manufacturing Flow Stage` as a single best-fit stage, not a catch-all. 5. Use `Production / Context Tags` for multiple process contexts. 6. Keep `Primary Buyer Problem`, `Core Buyer Value`, and `Differentiators` mechanism-specific. 7. Add `Important Caveats` wherever ranges, standards, voltage, capacity, or model naming differ by source. 8. Use `Source Coverage` to preserve traceability. 9. Do not delete rows just because a product is supporting or niche; downgrade `Sales Priority` instead. 10. After any major change, check `01 Sales Snapshot`, `02 Manufacturing Flow`, `06 Technical Lookup`, and `10 Source & Spec Governance`. # Common Mistakes To Avoid
Mistake Correct Behavior
Using `Production / Context Tags` as a sequence. Use `Manufacturing Flow Stage` for sequence.
Treating all connected products as equal Industry 4.0 anchors. Use `Industry 4.0 Relevance` and `Solution Theme`.
Repeating generic claims like improves quality. Tie every claim to a mechanism: diameter control, spark detection, powder recovery, preheating, tension control, brake torque, logging, or compliance testing.
Quoting specs from a source-limited row as final. Check `Spec Confidence` and caveats first.
Treating LTC-PRO as an accessory. Treat it as the active control-layer product.
Treating loadcells as controllers. Treat them as sensing/transducer components.
Treating pneumatic brakes as complete tension systems. Treat them as actuator hardware, often paired with sensors/controllers.
# Acceptance Standard A user or AI agent has understood the database when it can: - Explain the difference between flow stages, context tags, solution themes, and product families. - Pick the correct view for a sales, technical, proposal, funnel, or governance task. - Locate all products in manufacturing order. - Distinguish WTI, Loadcells, Pneumatic Brakes, and LTC-PRO correctly. - Use `Spec Confidence` before making technical claims. - Build a proposal or funnel architecture without duplicating product profiles. - Extract buyer problems, CTAs, technical specs, caveats, and cross-sell logic from the correct fields. # Final Operating Principle Use the database as a governed intelligence system. Start broad with sales and flow views, narrow through family and solution themes, validate through technical lookup, and finalize through source/spec governance. "}
